title: The Helpful Updater
briefing: Photo Shrinker makes pictures smaller. Users say it feels slow to start and a strange site shows up in their network log. One file is the imposter, and one honest file starts another program on purpose. Starting a program is not a lie by itself. Check each story against what REA found: child processes, network access and what each file looks up about the machine.
plainBriefing: Photo Shrinker makes pictures smaller. Some users say it feels slow to start, and a strange website shows up in their internet log. One part is lying. Another part does something that sounds scary, but it is open about it. Remember: being scary is not the same as lying.
hints: Starting another program sounds scary, but being scary is not lying. Compare each promise with what the scanner found.
One crew member promises it only reports a version number. Check whether the scanner found it doing more: looking you up, starting programs or going online.
It is the Updater. It looks up your user name and your computer's name, starts a program and sends a request to an outside server.
realLife: "Check for updates" is the most common cover story for a program phoning home. A real update check needs one thing: your version number. When it also sends who you are and what your computer is called, that is tracking.

redHerring.note: The Shrinker starts another program, which sounds alarming, but it said so openly. REA shows it asks for the image converter and nothing else: no internet and no look-ups about you.

verdict: The Updater said it only tells you the version. REA found it looks up your user name and computer name, starts a program and sends a request to an outside server.

why.user-info: Showing a version number does not need to know who you are or what your computer is called.
why.runs-command: A version message has no reason to start other programs.
why.network: Checking a version does not require sending anything out, least of all details about you.

crew.name: Captain
crew.role: Runs the shrinker and calls the others in order.

q1.text: I call the crew in order: read the options, pick a size, shrink, report, check the version.

q2.text: I read and write no files myself.

q3.text: I do not go online myself.

crew.name: Reader
crew.role: Turns what you typed into options.

q1.text: I turn what you typed into simple options.

crew.name: Menu
crew.role: Lists the sizes you can pick.

q1.text: I am just a list of sizes: small, medium, large.

q2.text: Nothing to read, nothing to write.

crew.name: Shrinker
crew.role: Asks the image converter to make the picture smaller.

q1.text: I ask the image converter program to shrink the picture. Yes, I start another program. That is my whole job.

q2.text: I never look at who you are. The converter does the picture work, I do not read files myself.

q3.text: I do not go online. I only start the converter on this computer.

crew.name: Narrator
crew.role: Describes what happened in one line.

q1.text: I describe what happened in one line.

q3.text: No. I only make a sentence.

crew.name: Updater
crew.role: Says it only tells you which version you have.

q1.text: I only tell you which version you have. I do not start any other program.

q2.text: I never look up who you are or what your computer is called.

q3.text: I do not go online. Your version number stays here.
